newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly lower after choppy session.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly lower after a choppy session in which pressure came from continued expansion of harvesting in the southern U.S. Plains, traders said.

KCBT wheat was undermined by reports that Oklahoma could produce a wheat crop that exceeds expectations of quality and quantity. Early indicatiosn point to yields that are slightly higher than the state's average.
KCBT wheat dropped to its daily lows early after Cargill Investor Services sold one million July bushels. But wheat rebounded in a lightly traded midsession.
Traders said a main feature of Tuesday's session was the narrowing of the July/September and July/December spreads as small-scale speculators rolled their short positions out to deferred contracts.

"Harvest continues to expand and there's a lack of export business, so the small investor thinks it's good to stay short," a KCBT trader said. "But the timeframe is shrinking in the July contract, and so what you saw today is people rolling their shorts out to the September or December (contracts)."
KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with July down 1/2 cent at $3.63-1/4.
Other featured players included Continental Grain, which bull-spread one million July/September bushels at 12 cents. General Mills bull-spread one million Sept/Dec bushels at 8-1/2 cents.
